reason: Connecting the motor neuron to the muscle junction should establish the pathway for signals to reach the muscles.
expectation: I expect a motor connection that can later be fitted to the arm.

alternatives.reason: The stretch-sensing pathway also supports the goal, but I chose the motor connection first.

effect: The motor pathway connects a nerve ending to a muscle fibre and explains how a signal can trigger contraction. I can now build a sensory pathway.
reaction: The link between the nerve signal, calcium and contraction was useful.
reason: Combining the muscle spindle with a sensory neuron should build the stretch-sensing pathway described in the goal.
expectation: I expect a sensory connection that can report muscle stretch and later join the arm and nervous system.

alternatives.reason: Adding touch-sensitive skin also advances the goal, but I chose to build the stretch pathway first.

effect: The stretch pathway now leads toward the spinal cord; I can move on to the touch pathway.
reaction: The result matched my expectation, though it added little explanation.
reason: Adding touch-sensitive skin to the arm is the only available combination and advances the remaining sensory connection.
expectation: I expect an arm with touch receptors that can later connect to sensory fibres.

effect: The arm now has slots for all three pathways, and the explanation distinguishes touch from muscle stretch sensing.
reaction: The connection between muscle stretch and limb position was useful.
reason: The motor pathway is ready, so I’ll fit it into the arm first.
expectation: I expect the motor pathway to fill the motor slot, leaving the sensory slots open.

alternatives.reason: The stretch pathway is also ready, but I chose to connect the motor pathway first.

effect: The motor pathway is fitted, leaving the stretch and touch connections to add.
reaction: The fitting was straightforward and added no new explanation.
reason: The stretch pathway is ready and fills one of the remaining slots.
expectation: I expect the stretch pathway to be fitted, leaving the touch slot open.

alternatives.reason: The touch fibres could also be fitted now, but I chose the completed stretch pathway first.

effect: The stretch pathway is fitted, leaving the touch connection to add.
reaction: The fitting was predictable and added no further explanation.
reason: The touch fibres fill the remaining slot, and this is the only available combination.
expectation: I expect the touch fibres to connect to the arm, completing its three pathway fittings.

effect: The touch fibres are fitted, completing the three pathway slots. The arm can now be connected to the brain and spinal cord.
reaction: The final fitting was predictable and added no further explanation.
reason: Connecting the completed arm to the brain and spinal cord directly serves the goal and is the only available combination.
expectation: I expect a responsive arm connected to the brain and spinal cord through its motor and sensory pathways.

effect: The completed arm shows sensory signals traveling toward the brain and spinal cord and motor signals traveling outward. The explanation connects sensory feedback to adjusting movement.
reaction: The final picture and explanation brought the separate pathways together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the arm to the brain and spinal cord was most worthwhile because the result showed how incoming sensory information and outgoing commands relate during movement.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the three pathways became repetitive: each result confirmed a placement but added little explanation.

surprise.text: The explanation that muscle stretch contributes to sensing limb position made the stretch pathway more meaningful to me.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt purposeless, though the order of the three pathway fittings seemed arbitrary.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter to see how the responsive arm connects to the rest of the body, though I would hope for fewer repetitive fittings.
